extracted.intended_audience: interested parties, petitioners, foreign governments, importers, respondents, counsel, and other stakeholders participating in federal administrative proceedings and notice-and-comment processes (trade remedy proceedings, NOAA EFP applicants, information-collection commenters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for participating in multiple Federal Register notices, including joining annual inquiry service lists, submitting scope rulings, responding to ministerial error corrections in antidumping reviews, applying for or commenting on Exempted Fishing Permits, and commenting on information-collection requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of Annual Inquiry Service List (AISL) in ACCESS
rubrics_metrics.description: For orders published after November 4, 2021, Commerce will create an annual inquiry service list segment in ACCESS within five business days of publication of the notice of the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each AISL is maintained in ACCESS under the case number and a specific segment type called 'AISL-Annual Inquiry Service List.' The segment will be combined with an SSI field pre-populated with the order's anniversary month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of appearance deadline to be on AISL
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties wishing to be added to the annual inquiry service list must submit an entry of appearance in the AISL segment in ACCESS within 30 days after the date of publication of the order in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commerce requests that law firms with multiple attorneys designate a lead attorney for inclusion. Commerce will finalize the AISL within five business days after the 30-day period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirement for scope rulings and circumvention inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested party submitting a scope ruling application or request for a circumvention inquiry must serve a copy of the application or request on the persons on the annual inquiry service list for that order and any companion order covering the same merchandise from the same country of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is required by the Final Rule and Procedural Guidance; related procedural notices and updates will be posted to ACCESS.

rubrics_metrics.name: AISL updates and amendment procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce may update an annual inquiry service list at any time based on amendments to entries of appearance to remove or modify members, representatives, or contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes or announcements pertaining to these procedures will be posted to the ACCESS website. Petitioners and foreign governments must amend their entries during annual update periods as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic continued placement for petitioners and foreign governments
rubrics_metrics.description: After an initial request and placement on the AISL, both petitioners and foreign governments will automatically be placed on the AISL in subsequent years and need not resubmit entries each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They are, however, responsible for making amendments to their entries of appearance during the annual update in accordance with the procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written-scope dispositive for AD/CVD orders (DOTP example)
rubrics_metrics.description: The written description of the scope of the orders is dispositive over CAS numbers or HTSUS classifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example scope language: DOTP covered regardless of form; blends included when constituent parts have not been chemically reacted to produce a different product; for commingled products, only the subject component is covered. CAS 6422-86-2 and HTSUS subheadings provided for convenience and customs purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of ministerial error (section 751(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'ministerial error' includes errors in addition, subtraction, or other arithmetic functions, clerical errors from inaccurate copying or duplication, and any other unintentional error the administering authority considers ministerial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For final results of administrative reviews, Commerce will analyze comments and, if appropriate, correct ministerial errors by amending the final results per 19 CFR 351.224(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for correcting ministerial errors in final results
rubrics_metrics.description: If Commerce agrees an allegation constitutes a ministerial error, it will amend the final results to correct the error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections are described in a Ministerial Error Memorandum placed on the record and corrections to margins and rates will be reflected in an amended final results notice. Commerce will disclose calculations performed in connection with amended final results to interested parties under administrative protective order within five days after public announcement or publication of the notice (19 CFR 351.224(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Importer-specific assessment rate calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: For a respondent (e.g., ACA), Commerce intends to calculate importer-specific antidumping assessment rates based on the ratio of the total amount of dumping calculated for each importer's examined sales to the total entered value of those sales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If actual entered value is not reported for all U.S. sales, Commerce will calculate importer-specific per-unit duty rates by dividing the importer’s aggregated amount of dumping for examined sales by the total quantity of those sales and will estimate entered value to compute an ad valorem rate to determine de minimis status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative per-unit assessment when entered value missing
rubrics_metrics.description: When a respondent has not reported entered value for all U.S. sales, importer-specific per-unit assessment rates may be calculated by dividing aggregated dumping by the total quantity of those sales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commerce estimates entered value for each U.S. sale to calculate an estimated ad valorem rate to check if the per-unit rate is de minimis.

rubrics_metrics.name: De minimis threshold and treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: A margin or assessment rate that is de minimis (i.e., less than 0.50 percent) will be treated as zero for cash deposit purposes and entries may be liquidated without regard to antidumping duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a respondent's weighted-average dumping margin is zero or de minimis, or an importer-specific (estimated) ad valorem assessment rate is zero or de minimis, Commerce intends to instruct CBP to liquidate appropriate entries without regard to antidumping duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment instructions timing and injunction hold
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce intends to issue assessment instructions to CBP no earlier than 35 days after publication of the amended final results; if a timely summons is filed at the U.S. Court of International Trade, instructions will direct CBP not to liquidate relevant entries until the time for parties to file a request for statutory injunction has expired (within 90 days of publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This controls the timing of assessment and possible judicial stays of liquidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquidation rule for entries where respondent did not know destination
rubrics_metrics.description: For entries of subject merchandise produced by an individually examined respondent for which it did not know its merchandise was destined for the United States, Commerce intends to instruct CBP to liquidate such entries at the all-others rate if there is no rate for the intermediate company(ies) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example all-others rate referenced is 16.92% from the LTFV Final Determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment rate for non-examined companies
rubrics_metrics.description: For companies not selected for individual examination, Commerce will instruct CBP to assess antidumping duties at the assessment rate equal to the weighted-average dumping margin for the non-examined companies in the (amended) final results of review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review-specific rate is applied uniformly to the list of non-examined companies provided in the appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash deposit rate determination rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon publication of the amended final results, cash deposit requirements are effective and determined as follows: (1) cash deposit rate for subject merchandise exported by companies listed equals the weighted-average dumping margin established in the amended final results (unless de minimis); (2) for exporters previously reviewed but not covered by this review, continue the company-specific rate from the most recent segment; (3) if exporter not covered but producer is, use producer's most recently-completed segment rate; (4) all other producers/exporters use the all-others rate established in the LTFV Final Determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These cash deposit requirements remain in effect until further notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importer certificate re reimbursement obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Importers are responsible under 19 CFR 351.402(f) to file a certificate regarding the reimbursement of antidumping duties prior to liquidation of the relevant entries during the review period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply could result in Commerce’s presumption that reimbursement occurred and subsequent assessment of double antidumping duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: APO materials return/destruction obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties subject to an Administrative Protective Order (APO) must return or destroy proprietary information disclosed under APO in accordance with 19 CFR 351.305(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely written notification of return, destruction, or conversion to a judicial protective order is requested; failure to comply is a sanctionable violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow OMB guidance for customer surveys (NOAA NWS)
rubrics_metrics.description: NOAA’s NWS customer satisfaction and feedback collection follows guidelines in the OMB Resource Manual for Customer Surveys and Executive Order 12862.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the generic clearance, offices use an approved question bank and may select subsets tailored to their programs; proposed questionnaires are submitted to OMB via a fast-track process without separate FRNs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on surveying regulated entities (NOAA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The generic clearance will not be used to survey bodies NOAA regulates unless precautions ensure respondents believe they face no risk for not responding or for content of responses (e.g., names and addresses not required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protective steps must be taken to avoid perceived coercion or regulatory risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey question types and intended uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Two sets of survey questions are used: quantitative (numerical satisfaction ratings on product/service quality, staff courtesy, format/documentation) to identify needs for improvement; and qualitative (who uses the product/service, how it's used, preferred format/medium) to inform program decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offices select relevant questions from the bank to create program-level questionnaires and can develop new questionnaires as needed under the generic clearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFP application completeness and notice/comment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An EFP application that contains all required information warrants further consideration and must be published to provide interested parties opportunity to comment (Magnuson-Stevens Act requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Federal Register notice includes the preliminary determination that the application is complete, specifies the exemptions requested, provides a public comment deadline, and supplies submission instructions (email, subject line, acceptance of anonymous comments).

rubrics_metrics.name: EFP requested regulatory exemptions and project summary
rubrics_metrics.description: The EFP request must identify the CFR citations and regulations from which participating vessels would be exempted and provide a project summary including objectives, project location, number of vessels, number/duration of trips, gear type, and expected data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables in the notice spell out the specific regulations and the 'need for exemption' justification (e.g., increasing skate wing trip limits to assess utilization).

rubrics_metrics.name: EFP data collection and monitoring requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All participating vessels under the EFP must collect data on all large-mesh gillnet trips fished with and without the increased trip limit, including trip duration, number of nets set and soak time, quantity and value of skate catch and non-target catch, fuel used, and monkfish/bycatch data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch data will be compared between trips with and without the increased trip limit to inform project objectives and assess economic/ecological consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFP precautionary trigger and suspension condition
rubrics_metrics.description: If skate landings surpass 75 percent of total allowable landings (TAL) in either season, the possession limit exemption would be suspended for the remainder of that season and vessels would be subject to the fishery-wide possession limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 75% trigger is intended to be precautionary; the notice gives TAL and estimates of additional landings under the EFP.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFP modifications/extensions criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor modifications and extensions to an approved EFP may be granted without further notice if they are essential to facilitate completion of the research and have minimal impacts that do not change the scope or impact of the initially approved request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any fishing activity outside the scope of the exempted activity is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: CFPB information-collection comment requests and required comment topics
rubrics_metrics.description: For information-collection notices, the CFPB requests comments on: (a) whether the collection is necessary and will have practical utility; (b) the accuracy of the burden estimate and methods used; (c) ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information; and (d) ways to minimize respondent burden including use of technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must be submitted by specified deadlines via listed methods, will become public records (avoid including sensitive personal information), and will be summarized/included in OMB approval requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection burden and respondent details
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices specify OMB control numbers, type of request (new/extension/revision), affected public categories, estimated number of respondents, average hours per response, and total annual burden hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These estimates and collection instruments are made available for review (e.g., via reginfo.gov) and commenters are asked to address the PRA burden and utility questions above.
